title: The Blind Man and the Cub
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: There was once a Blind Man who had so fine a sense of touch that, when any animal was put into his hands, he could tell what it was merely by the feel of it. One day the Cub of a Wolf was put into his hands, and he was asked what it was. He felt it for some time, and then said, "Indeed, I am not sure whether it is a Wolf's Cub or a Fox's: but this I know--it would never do to trust it in a sheepfold."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what special ability does the Blind Man have?
options: The ability to hear an animal's heartbeat
A keen sense of smell for tracking animals
A fine sense of touch that lets him identify animals
The ability to guess an animal's age exactly

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what animal's Cub is placed in the Blind Man's hands?
options: A Wolf's
A Fox's
A Bear's
A Lion's

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Blind Man asked to do once the Cub is in his hands?
options: Guess how old it is
Decide whether to keep it
Describe what color its fur is
Say what animal it is

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what two animals does the Blind Man consider the Cub might belong to?
options: A Wolf or a Dog
A Wolf or a Fox
A Fox or a Cat
A Dog or a Bear

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Blind Man say it would never do to trust the Cub near?
options: A henhouse
A stable full of horses
A sheepfold
A basket of fish

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Blind Man unsure whether the Cub is a Wolf's or a Fox's?
options: The two kinds of cub apparently feel similar enough to be mistaken for one another
He has never touched either kind of animal before
The Cub refuses to hold still while he feels it
He believes someone has switched the Cub without telling him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Blind Man sense about the Cub despite his uncertainty over its exact kind?
options: That it is too young to survive without its mother
That it belongs to someone in the village nearby
That it will grow to be unusually large
That it already shows signs of being dangerous to sheep

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "sheepfold" mean in the Blind Man's warning?
options: A tool used for shearing wool
An enclosure where sheep are kept
A market where sheep are sold
A path used to herd animals

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "merely" mean in "merely by the feel of it"?
options: Rarely, almost never
Slowly, taking great care
Simply, using nothing more than
Loudly, without any doubt

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: A dangerous nature can be recognized even before it is fully grown
Blind people are always better judges of character than sighted ones
Wolves and foxes should never be kept as pets
Touch is a more reliable sense than sight in every situation

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Blind Man usually identify an animal?
options: By listening to the sounds it makes
By smelling it closely
By asking others to describe it
By the feel of it in his hands

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how long does the Blind Man feel the Cub before answering?
options: Only for an instant
For some time
For the whole afternoon
Until it fell asleep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the one thing the Blind Man says he does know for certain?
options: That the Cub belongs to a Wolf, not a Fox
That the Cub is still very young
That it would never do to trust the Cub in a sheepfold
That the Cub has recently been fed

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Blind Man's warning matter even though he cannot name the Cub's exact species?
options: Both possible species he names would pose the same danger to sheep
He is certain the Cub belongs to neither a Wolf nor a Fox
He believes the Cub cannot survive without its mother nearby
He assumes someone will simply ask the Cub's owner directly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Blind Man's fine sense of touch allow him to notice that sight alone might miss?
options: The exact color of the Cub's fur
How far the Cub has traveled that day
Whether the Cub has been fed recently
Subtle qualities in the Cub that hint at its future danger

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "tendencies" mean in the closing line "Evil tendencies are early shown"?
options: Physical marks or scars on the body
Natural inclinations or leanings toward certain behavior
Formal agreements between two parties
Loud sounds made to warn others

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Blind Man mistakes a Cub for a full-grown Wolf
A Blind Man refuses to touch the Cub at all
A Blind Man senses danger in a young Cub even without knowing its exact kind
A Blind Man is bitten by the Cub while examining it
